question:
A diffraction-limited optical system has a circular aperture of diameter $D=5.0\,\text{cm}$. It is used to observe two distant point sources separated by an angular distance $\Delta\theta=1.40\times10^{-5}\,\text{rad}$.

The observation is repeated with monochromatic light of wavelengths $\lambda_1=500\,\text{nm}$ and $\lambda_2=650\,\text{nm}$.

Using the Rayleigh criterion for a circular aperture, decide for each wavelength whether the two sources are just resolved or not, and identify which wavelength provides better angular resolution.

options.A: Resolved at $\lambda_1$ but not resolved at $\lambda_2$ (better resolution at $\lambda_1$)
options.B: Resolved at $\lambda_2$ but not resolved at $\lambda_1$ (better resolution at $\lambda_2$)
options.C: Resolved at both wavelengths (better resolution at $\lambda_2$)
